root.claim: A deterministic fixed-tape Turing machine multiplies two $n$-bit integers exactly in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time, with $\kappa=2^{-182}$.
root.method: reduce the product to a convolution evaluated by Fourier-type transforms, make the two bottlenecks (address movement and butterfly layers) cheaper by recursive linear networks, then assemble the exact algorithm and total the cost

motivation.text: Scanning an array at each of $\Theta(\log n)$ transform levels already costs $\Theta(n\log n)$, so both movement and arithmetic must be made cheaper.

quote.quote: We therefore need savings in both movement and arithmetic.

root.salient: The saving is a strict power of the logarithm, $(\lg n)^{-\kappa}$, even though $\kappa=2^{-182}$ is astronomically small: the algorithm beats $n\log n$ in the model where $n\log n$ was conjectured optimal.
